newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NEW ZEALAND INVESTMENT PROPERTY IN DEMAND - REINZ.
newsitem.headline: NEW ZEALAND INVESTMENT PROPERTY IN DEMAND - REINZ.

text.p: Demand for central business district investment property in the major centres continued in the June quarter, the Real Estate Institute of New Zealand (REINZ) said on Thursday.
"The latest quarterly survey shows lower interest rates during the quarter helped stimulate demand for industrial and commercial property," Kent Prier of REINZ said.

Auckland cbd properties were subject to strong investor interest and they traded at average capitalisation rates -- a measure of return on capital -- of 7.5 to 10 percent, compared with a range of eight to 12 percent in the March quarter.
Good investment properties were in high demand, with a shortage of quality listings recorded in most regions.

In particular, industrial property was in short supply, with levels of enquiry outweighing the amount of quality property available. Of note was the level of interest expressed by owner/operators in this sector.

"Good investment properties -- both commercial and industrial -- are attracting strong buyer attention. Returns over the last quarter have remained higher than interest rates, however it is unclear whether this will continue to be the case given the recent increases in interest rates," Prier said.
Profitable businesses in the higher price range were in strong demand, compared to a low level of enquiry for smaller businesses.
